brief_summary: Two horizontal timeline bars. Top bar (QMK) starts at a wired-firmware origin point in 2015 and shows a shorter, later amber segment where Bluetooth support was added board by board. Bottom bar (ZMK) starts at a Bluetooth-plus-Zephyr origin point in 2018 and runs wireless-native the full length of the bar. Illustrates the article's 'bolted-on versus built-in' argument.
data_sources: zmk-wireless-split-firmware-guide.mdx § 'Why QMK's wireless story is the weaker one' — 'QMK was not designed around wireless. It grew up as a wired firmware ... Bluetooth support was added later, board by board, largely through community-maintained modules rather than a first-class subsystem.'

zmk-wireless-split-firmware-guide.mdx § 'Why QMK's wireless story is the weaker one' — 'ZMK made the opposite bet from day one. It sits on Zephyr, an RTOS built for low-power embedded devices generally, and its event-driven scanning and sleep architecture were designed around the assumption that the device runs on a coin cell or a small lithium-polymer pack.'
